An agent acts; a chat window only advises. a routine change and check it. *⏱ ~30 minutes · Start on `main`, Git pane clean, Claude Code running in Manual mode.* :::{#block3-files .callout-note collapse="true"} ## This block's files, and how it fits This block uses the same repository, branch and data as Block 2, with nothing to download. What is new is that the agent now changes files. There is no checkpoint for this block alone: `checkpoint-skills`, at the end of Block 4, holds its files. | File | Where it comes from | Used in | |---|---|---| | `data/raw/voles_metabolism.csv` | Shipped: the data from Block 2 | Exercises 1 and 2 | | `scripts/explore_voles.R` (it sources `scripts/functions/load_voles.R`) | Shipped: loads the data into `voles` | Exercise 2: the agent adds `mass_change_g` to `voles` | | `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/settings.json` | Shipped: the instruction file, and the settings that start Claude Code in Manual mode; you edit the first in Block 4 and test the second in Block 5 | Throughout | | `tests/test_explore.R`, `tests/test_ai_log.R` | Shipped: check the agent's column and plot script, and the form of your log line | Exercise 2, step 5 | | `scripts/explore_mass_change_plot.R`, and the figure it saves in `outputs/` (which git ignores) | The agent writes the script in Exercise 2, step 2; the tests run it in step 5 | Exercise 2 | | `docs/ai-log.md` | You, in Exercise 2, step 4 | Every block from now on | ::: ## Exercise 1: What can it see? :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Name the routes (3 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** see exactly what reached the model provider when the agent investigated in Block 2, so that you can name every route your data take. **Start state:** Claude Code running in the Terminal tab, as you left it in Block 2. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Using another tool The exercises use Claude Code. With **Posit Assistant**: - **Exercise 1:** scroll back to your Block 2 conversation in the same way. R code it ran in your session is route 4. Every request also carries the names and types of your objects (route 3), though no action in the transcript shows it. - **Exercise 2:** use `/plan` for step 1 and Normal mode (`/normal`) for step 2. The checks are the same: the Git pane and the R console. For **GitHub Copilot**, see *GitHub Copilot and the remote rung* in *Going further*. ::: **1. Find the transcript.** Scroll back in Claude Code to Block 2's Exercise 1, where the agent read `data/raw/voles_metabolism.csv` and ran `Rscript`. Above each reply, Claude Code lists the actions it took. If you cleared the conversation, re-run that prompt from [Block 2](11c-debugging.qmd). **2. Name each route** in the diagram below. A file it read is route 2. The output of a command it ran is route 4. What you pasted yourself, in Block 2's Exercise 2 prompt, is route 1. Then add two routes that no action shows. One is `AGENTS.md`, which Claude Code reads at the start of every conversation (route 2). The other is the context it adds itself, including your recent commit messages (route 3). **You are done when** you can name every file or command output that reached the model provider. **If it goes wrong:** if the transcript shows files you did not expect, or a search of the project, name those too: an agent reads what it judges useful, which is why the habits below matter for confidential data. :::: ::: :::::: {.dia .dia-lanes role="figure" aria-label="Four routes by which data reach the model provider: 1, what you paste, in any tool; 2, project files the tool reads; 3, context the tool adds itself: Claude Code adds the project folder, platform, date and a snapshot of git status with recent commit messages, and Posit Assistant adds the R version and the names and types of your objects, not their values; 4, the output of commands the agent runs"} ::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Route 1: what you paste ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-you} Errors, output and results you paste into a chat or prompt ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} any tool ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-plain} Model provider ::: ::::: ::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Route 2: files it reads ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-file} Copilot: open files. Claude Code and Posit Assistant: any project file they choose to read ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} read ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-plain} Model provider ::: ::::: ::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Route 3: context the tool adds itself ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-plain} Claude Code: project folder, platform, date, and a snapshot of git status with recent commit messages. Posit Assistant: R version, and the names and types of your objects (not their values) ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} Claude Code, Posit Assistant ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-plain} Model provider ::: ::::: ::::: {.dia-flow} ::: {.dia-label} Route 4: output of commands it runs ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-ai} The agent runs `Rscript` or `head data.csv`, and reads what it prints ::: ::: {.dia-arrow} Claude Code, Posit Assistant ::: ::: {.dia-node .dia-plain} Model provider ::: ::::: ::: {.dia-caption} Everything before an arrow reaches the model provider: any data file in the project the agent reads, and any values its code prints. ::: :::::: ::::{.callout-important} ## Working with confidential data: five habits 1. **Work on a copy.** Put a synthetic or anonymised copy in the project, and run the final analysis on the real data yourself, outside the agent's folder. 2. **Know your account.** Commercial accounts (Team, Enterprise, API) are not used for model training. On Pro or Max, set `/privacy-settings`. Check your institution's approval, ethics approval and data agreements first. 3. **Deny reads of sensitive folders** in `/permissions`, for example `Read(/data/confidential/**)`. It stops Claude Code's own file reads and simple commands such as `cat`, but not R code that opens the file itself. 4. **Stay in Manual mode,** but remember that it does not ask before read-only commands such as `head` and `cat`. Keep confidential files out of the project (habit 1). 5. **Describe, don't show.** `names()` and `dim()` describe the data without showing values. `summary()` prints real minima and maxima. `print()`, `glimpse()` and `str()` print actual rows. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## How it works: tool notes There is no `.claudeignore` file, and `/sandbox` is not available on native Windows. Posit Assistant blocks `.Renviron` and `.env` by default. It shares the names and types of objects in your session, not their values, but code it runs can still print values. ::: :::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Context you hold in your head (instructor demonstration) An assistant's answer about your data is only as good as its context. It is reliable only when it has real information, such as something you pasted, a file it read, or output from a command it ran. In Block 2 you mostly pasted that information yourself; once, you let the agent fetch it. Either way, everything it uses leaves your machine. A data file supplies column names, but not your question or your design. Your instructor asks a new chat: **Prompt (browser chat):** ```text I have a dataset with pre and post measurements. How should I analyse it? ``` and then, in another new chat: **Prompt (browser chat):** ```text I have 72 voles, balanced across three treatment arms (Control, Low_dose, High_dose) and two sexes (M, F). Each animal has body mass measured before and after treatment, and a single post-treatment metabolic-rate reading. My question is whether the high-dose treatment changes mass relative to control, and whether the effect differs between sexes. The dataset is small (n = 12 per cell). I will report effect sizes alongside any inferential test. Given this design, what is a defensible primary analysis, and what are the main threats to its validity? ``` The first gets a tour of options. The second can get a recommendation, because the design now exists outside your head. Treat it as a proposal to check: the primary analysis is your decision. To try it yourself, see *Going further*. ::: ## Exercise 2: What can it do? The model is the same at every rungOne level of the autonomy ladder in Block 3, from suggesting a line (rung 0) to acting with no prompts (rung 5). Each step up removes a moment when you would have seen an action before it happened. of the autonomy ladder. What changes is its permission modeThe setting that decides how much Claude Code may do without asking: plan (read only), default (asks before edits and commands), acceptEdits (edits without asking) and bypassPermissions (never asks).: what it may do without asking. Rung 3, act with approval, is where routine work is safe: - you start from a commit, so you can revert any change; - you see every edit and command first; - a test checks the result, whatever the agent reports. :::{.callout-note} ## The autonomy ladder An assistant that advises leaves you to filter every change. An agent that acts removes that filter, unless you put it back. The rungs differ in how much of that filtering is left to you. | Rung | What happens | Claude Code | Posit Assistant | |---|---|---|---| | 0. Suggest | Completes the line you are typing | — | Next Edit Suggestions | | 1. Ask | Answers; changes nothing | — (no ask mode; Block 2's answer-only line is a request) | Ask mode (`/ask`) | | 2. Plan | Proposes steps; changes nothing until you approve | `/plan` | `/plan` | | 3. Act, with approval | Edits files and runs commands, asking first | Manual (`default`): the workshop's starting mode | Normal mode | | 4. Act, partly unsupervised | Some actions without asking | `acceptEdits`; `auto` (a classifier approves actions) | Auto mode (`/auto`) | | 5. Act, unsupervised | No prompts | `bypassPermissions` | YOLO mode (`/yolo`) | From rung 3 up, what changes is which tool callsA single action an agent takes, such as reading a file, editing a file or running a shell command. Permission rules and hooks act on tool calls. run without your approval. [Block 6](11k-build-an-agent.qmd), after lunch, builds that approval step in code. Your workshop repository starts Claude Code in **Manual**, although recent versions of Claude Code start in `auto`. Keep Manual for confidential data. `/plan` can still run commands, so read any it proposes. Use only rungs 0 to 3 today. The [quick reference](11-AI-programming-integrated.qmd#cc-quick-reference) lists the commands for the other modes. Each rung up removes a moment when you would have seen the action. In `acceptEdits`, for example, file commands such as `cp` and `mv` run without asking, so a `cp` over a raw data file needs no approval. The higher the rung, the more an agent acts on its guesses about your conventions. That is why [Block 4](11e-instructions-skills.qmd) writes them down. ::: :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Ask, plan, act (15 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** have the agent add a column and a plot script at rung 3, then check its work with the diff and the tests, so that you trust the change because you checked it, not because the agent reported it. **Start state:** your workshop repository on `main`, Git pane clean, Claude Code in Manual mode. Check its work from the R console and the Git pane ([checking work](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd#checking-work)). **1. Plan (rung 2).** In Claude Code, type `/clear`, then: **Prompt (Claude Code):** ```text /plan In scripts/explore_voles.R, add a mass_change_g column (mass_post_g minus mass_pre_g) to the voles data frame itself. Create a new script scripts/explore_mass_change_plot.R that plots mass_change_g by treatment_arm and saves the figure to outputs/ with ggsave(). Don't run anything; I'll check the scripts myself. ``` Before you approve, check that the plan names both files, adds the column to `voles` itself, leaves `data/raw/` alone and saves the figure to `outputs/`. If anything is missing, choose **No, keep planning** and say what to change. **2. Act, with approval (rung 3).** Choose **Yes, manually approve edits**. It is not the first option: the first, *Yes, and use auto mode* (or *Yes, auto-accept edits*), switches the approvals off. Then read each edit before you approve it. **Answer each request with plain Yes or No.** Never choose an option that says *don't ask again*: it saves a rule that skips the question from then on. If it asks to run `git status` before it edits (`AGENTS.md` asks it to check), answer Yes: that command only reads. It may also ask to run the new scripts and the test suite with `Rscript`. Approve a run only if you can say what it does and why you want it now; refusing is always safe. For these, choose **No**: you check the result yourself next. **3. Read the diff.** Click **Diff** in the Git pane for each changed file. Read it as you would a colleague's work: the diff shows every change, including any you did not ask for. **4. Record.** Create `docs/ai-log.md` (`usethis::edit_file("docs/ai-log.md")`). Write the first line of your AI-use logA record written at the time of each piece of AI-assisted work, in the form: date; tool and model; task; what you kept or changed. It becomes the AI declaration in a README. yourself, on one line, in the form from Block 1. Don't copy the example: use today's date, as YYYY-MM-DD, and the model name shown above the Claude Code prompt. ```text 2026-10-19; Claude Code (model as shown above the Claude Code prompt); added mass_change_g and a plot script; kept both after reading the diff ``` Writing it before you test means the tests check it too. **5. Test, then commit.** Restart R (*Session → Restart R*) so that nothing left in your session can make a test pass. Then run: **In the R console:** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} testthat::test_dir(here::here("tests")) ``` ::: The tests check that: - `mass_change_g` in `voles` really is post minus pre; - the plot script saves a figure in `outputs/` from a fresh R session; - your log line has four parts and a real date. Tests for later blocks skip. Commit the log and both scripts together (git ignores `outputs/`). **You are done when** you have read every line of the diff, the tests show no failures, the `explore` and `ai_log` lines of the test output show their tests under **OK**, not **S** (skipped), and your first log line is committed with both scripts. **If it goes wrong:** select the unwanted change in the Git pane and click **Revert**, then ask again more clearly. If `test_explore.R` says `voles` has no `mass_change_g`, the agent made the column somewhere else: ask it to add the column to `voles` itself. An **S** on `explore` or `ai_log` means its file is missing or misnamed. Out of time? Carry on: at the end of Block 4, `checkpoint-skills` holds this block's files (commit or discard your changes in the Git pane first, so the switch is not blocked). :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Stretch: reflect on the rungs At which rung did you decide the most? Where would you have missed an unwanted change without the diff? **Payoff.** What did the agent do, how long did checking it take, and would you automate this again? ::: :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## At the command line The same checks from a terminal (after `/exit`, or in a second Terminal tab): `git status`, `git diff`, and `Rscript -e "testthat::test_dir('tests')"`. ::: :::: ::: :::{#safe-recipe .callout-note} ## The safe vibe-coding recipe 1. **Commit**, so you start from a clean Git pane. 2. **Protect the inputs:** `/permissions` shows the deny rules, or you add one. 3. **Have the checks ready:** tests in `tests/` before the agent starts. 4. **Ask** in one prompt or skill, in Manual mode, reading each approval. 5. **Run the checks:** the test suite in a fresh R session. 6. **Read the diff** in the Git pane, then commit or revert. You will use these six steps in Blocks 7 and 8. The template ships the protections and the tests, so most of the work is checking that they are there. ::: :::{.callout-note} ## Check · Reproduce · Record - **You can now:** hand an agent a routine multi-file change at rung 3, **trusted because** you read every diff and a test you did not write checks the result. - **Check:** the Git pane's diff after every agent action; the agent's report that something "still runs" is a claim until a test confirms it. - **Reproduce:** work only in a committed, clean repository, so every change is a diff you can inspect or revert. - **Record:** your AI-use log starts here, in `docs/ai-log.md`. ::: ## Check your understanding **You paste nothing, yet Claude Code names your columns correctly. How could it know them?**
**In Claude Code's acceptEdits mode, what does the agent do without asking?**
**Which check still works whatever rung the agent ran at?**
## Going further (not covered live) This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if it is useful to you. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Access and cost Plans and prices change; check before the session. - **Claude Code** needs an Anthropic account, used through a subscription or an API key; see Anthropic's documentation for current options. - **Posit Assistant** uses Posit AI Pass or your own provider key, including an Anthropic API key. In RStudio, providers are configured in the assistant's settings. - **GitHub Copilot** bills in AI credits; check GitHub's plans page for what your plan includes. - **Your institution** may have approved some of these tools and not others. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Trusting a repository's configuration Project settings and hooks are code that runs on your machine. A cloned repository can carry its own, so trust only repositories whose configuration you have read. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## GitHub Copilot and the remote rung Copilot offers the same ladder, plus a rung 6: its cloud agent works on your repository on GitHub, on its own branch, and returns a pull request. The self-study page [Self-study: Hand a task to GitHub Copilot's cloud agent](11l-copilot-cloud-agent.qmd) walks through it. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Stretch: the same error at three levels of context The code `voles |> mutate(mass_change_g = mass_post - mass_pre_g)` fails with "object 'mass_post' not found". In three new browser chats, ask about it with more context each time. First give the error message alone. Then give the error plus the code. Last, give the error, the code and the output of `glimpse(voles)`. With the code, a chat may guess `mass_post_g` by analogy with `mass_pre_g`, but only the `glimpse()` output lets it confirm the name. Column names you never supplied, or a famous dataset you never mentioned (`penguins`, `mtcars`), are signs it is guessing. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Exercise: context you hold in your head To try the demonstration above yourself, give the first prompt to a new browser chat. Give the second to another new chat, then compare the answers. A data file can supply column names and types, but not your scientific question or your design intent. ::: ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
agent An assistant that can read across a project's files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises.
AI-use log A record written at the time of each piece of AI-assisted work, in the form: date; tool and model; task; what you kept or changed. It becomes the AI declaration in a README.
assistant Any AI tool that helps you write or understand code, from inline completion to a chat window. In this course "assistant" is the general word; "agent" is used when the tool acts on your files.
permission mode The setting that decides how much Claude Code may do without asking: plan (read only), default (asks before edits and commands), acceptEdits (edits without asking) and bypassPermissions (never asks).
rung One level of the autonomy ladder in Block 3, from suggesting a line (rung 0) to acting with no prompts (rung 5). Each step up removes a moment when you would have seen an action before it happened.
tool call A single action an agent takes, such as reading a file, editing a file or running a shell command. Permission rules and hooks act on tool calls.
````` ::: ::: ## References - Claude Code documentation: *Permission modes*, . - Posit Assistant documentation: *Getting Started*, ; *Permissions & Trust*, . - GitHub documentation: *Plans for GitHub Copilot*, .
